name: Raene's Cleansing
summary: In Astranaar, Raene's Cleansing reaches its end as you return with Ran Bloodtooth's skull. The search began with Teronis and now leaves Ashenvale's furbolg threat diminished.

sections.title: A Bitter Trophy
sections.body: After Ran Bloodtooth falls, Krolg sends you back to Astranaar. You carry the chieftain's severed skull to Sentinel Raene Wolfrunner, proof that the threat prowling the forest depths has been struck down.

sections.title: In Memory of Teronis
sections.body: Raene Wolfrunner sets Ran Bloodtooth's skull beside Dartol's Rod in a place of reverence. The grim token honors Teronis, whose investigation into cleansing the corrupted furbolgs began this desperate effort.

faq.answer: Ran Bloodtooth was the fiercest corrupted furbolg threat in Ashenvale's forests. His defeat removes a chieftain who preyed on the woodland.

faq.q: Why does Raene Wolfrunner want the skull?
aliases: what does raene do with the skull
faq.answer: Raene Wolfrunner keeps Ran Bloodtooth's skull beside Dartol's Rod to honor victory and remember the danger overcome. The skull proves that the Sentinel forces and their allies struck down a mortal threat to Ashenvale.
Teronis was a night elf investigator whose death early in the search spurred the hunt for the cleansing gemstones and Dartol's Rod. Finishing the work carries forward his unfinished mission.
You complete the work in Astranaar by speaking with Sentinel Raene Wolfrunner, in Ashenvale's main night elf settlement.
Krolg is an ally who sends you to carry Ran Bloodtooth's severed skull back to Astranaar, where your people can recognize the victory.
Dartol's Rod is an enchanted relic assembled during the chain of events. It has deep magical ties to furbolg nature and cleansing.

angles.text: As a night elf, ending Ran Bloodtooth's fury honors fallen allies such as Teronis and helps reclaim Ashenvale's sacred groves.
As an Alliance member, delivering Bloodtooth's skull shows your people's commitment to defending Astranaar alongside the night elf Sentinels.
